title: Timing belt replacement
statusNote: Educational overview. The phase order and page locators come from a third-party mirror of RM718U and have not been checked against a licensed copy. No torque, force or dimension values are entered. Use the licensed factory manual for every sub-step, specification and diagram.

tools.name: RM718U repair manual (licensed copy)
tools.detail: Required for specifications, diagrams and full sub-steps.

tools.name: Torque wrench
tools.detail: Range depends on specifications not yet entered.

tools.name: Press for tensioner compression
tools.detail: Force limit not entered. Compress slowly.

tools.name: Coolant drain pan and funnel
tools.detail: Coolant capacity and type not entered.

parts.name: Timing belt
parts.note: OEM part number must come from the Lexus EPC for the production range.

parts.name: Timing belt idler (if inspection fails)
parts.note: Replacement criteria are in the inspection pages.

parts.name: Hydraulic tensioner (if inspection fails)
parts.note: Replacement criteria are in the inspection pages.

parts.name: Replacement seals and gaskets specified by the manual
parts.note: The installation pages specify replacement seals and adhesive. Exact items not entered.

checklist.text: Confirm that the vehicle is a 2000 US GS300 with the 2JZ-GE VVT-i. This guide does not apply to non-VVT-i 2JZ-GE or 2JZ-GTE engines.
Have the licensed RM718U timing-belt chapter and its linked cooling and charging pages available.
Plan the work on a cold engine.
Collect the tools listed below and look up every value the manual specifies for them.
Source the replacement belt and any parts that inspection may require by part number from the OEM catalog.

cautions.text: Moving the crankshaft or camshafts with the belt removed can allow piston-to-valve contact. Follow the factory positioning sequence.
Do not loosen the factory-set bolts on the VVT-i camshaft timing pulley.

steps.title: Under-cover and coolant
instructions: Remove the engine under-cover.
Drain the engine coolant as described in the linked cooling-system page.

cautions.text: Hot coolant is under pressure. Work on a cold engine.

completionChecks.text: Under-cover removed and fasteners stored.
Coolant drained into a container.

gaps: Drain plug location and coolant capacity not entered.

steps.title: Radiator assembly
instructions: Remove the radiator assembly following the linked cooling-system procedure (CO-18).
Disconnect the radiator hoses and the connections listed there before lifting the radiator out.

completionChecks.text: Radiator assembly removed and openings protected from debris.

gaps: The radiator assembly is shown as one grouped model. Fans, shroud and cooler lines are not separated.

steps.title: Accessory drive belt
instructions: Release the accessory belt tensioner and remove the accessory drive belt (linked CH-1).
The accessory belt is separate from the timing belt. It drives external accessories and does not set valve timing.

completionChecks.text: Accessory belt removed. Routing noted for reinstallation.

gaps: Accessory belt routing in the model is illustrative and must not be used as a routing diagram.

steps.title: Power-steering pump and front bracket
instructions: Detach the power-steering pump and its front bracket as the factory access sequence describes.
Check in the manual whether the pump stays connected to its lines and is set aside. The model only moves it out of view.

completionChecks.text: Pump and bracket clear of the upper timing cover. Hoses supported and not kinked.

gaps: Whether lines are disconnected is not established.
Pump and bracket positions are estimated.

steps.title: Upper timing cover and accessory tensioner
instructions: Remove the upper timing belt cover(s).
Remove the accessory belt tensioner so the crankshaft pulley can be reached.

completionChecks.text: Both camshaft timing pulleys are visible.

gaps: The source lists cover bolt groups of 5, 3 and 4. Their mapping to individual covers is unresolved, so cover bolts are not modeled.
Numbering of the upper covers (No.2/No.3) is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Loosen the crankshaft pulley bolt
instructions: Hold the crankshaft pulley with the specified holding tool and loosen the pulley bolt.
Do not remove the pulley yet. The factory sequence positions the engine first.

cautions.text: Use the holding tool. Do not hold the crankshaft through the timing belt or pulleys.

completionChecks.text: Crankshaft pulley bolt loosened, pulley still in place.

steps.title: Set the removal position
instructions: Set the engine to the factory compression reference, then rotate it to the removal position shown in EM-17.
Compare the real crankshaft and camshaft marks with the factory diagrams. Model teeth and pulley angles are not timing references.

specifications.label: Removal crankshaft position
specifications.note: Read from a third-party mirror. Confirm the exact position, marks and rotation direction in the licensed manual.

cautions.text: Incorrect crankshaft position with the belt disengaged can allow piston-to-valve contact.

completionChecks.text: Crankshaft and camshaft marks match the factory diagram for removal.

gaps: Timing mark geometry is not modeled.

steps.title: Remove the hydraulic tensioner
instructions: Remove the two hydraulic tensioner bolts and the tensioner with its dust boot.
Disconnect the timing belt from the camshaft timing pulleys.

completionChecks.text: Tensioner, boot and both bolts removed and kept together.

gaps: The tensioner and idler location is estimated. It is placed on the belt's slack side, inferred from clockwise crankshaft rotation.

steps.title: Camshaft pulleys and VVT-i oil hardware
instructions: The full factory chapter removes the camshaft timing pulleys, provides intake and head-cover access, and removes the VVT-i oil hardware.
Leave the factory-set bolts on the VVT-i pulley untouched.

cautions.text: Do not loosen the factory-set VVT-i pulley bolts.

completionChecks.text: The VVT-i pulley's factory-set bolts were not disturbed.

gaps: Whether this step is required for a belt-only replacement is not established here.
VVT-i oil hardware is one grouped model.

steps.title: Lower drive, belt and idler
instructions: Remove the crankshaft pulley, the No.1 (lower) timing cover and the belt guide.
Remove the timing belt, then the idler and the crankshaft timing pulley as the chapter describes.

cautions.text: Do not twist, fold or turn the belt inside out, and keep oil and water off it.

completionChecks.text: Belt, idler, guide and crankshaft timing pulley removed and laid out in order.

gaps: The source transcription lists one idler. Whether a second idler exists on this configuration is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Inspect belt, idler and tensioner
instructions: Inspect the belt for damage or contamination and find the cause of any abnormal wear.
Check that the idler turns smoothly. Inspect the hydraulic tensioner for leakage, pushrod resistance and the specified protrusion. Apply the manual's replacement criteria.

completionChecks.text: Belt condition recorded.
Idler rotation checked.
Tensioner leakage, resistance and protrusion checked against the manual.

gaps: The viewer cannot assess bearing condition, belt wear or protrusion.

steps.title: Install the lower drive
instructions: On a cold engine, install the keyed crankshaft timing pulley, its retaining plate and the idler.
Place the clean belt on the lower drive, then fit the guide, the No.1 cover and the crankshaft pulley.

completionChecks.text: Crankshaft timing pulley seated on its key.
Idler turns freely after tightening.

gaps: The retaining plate's position is estimated.

steps.title: Install the camshaft pulleys
instructions: Install the VVT-i pulley and its oil hardware, then the exhaust camshaft timing pulley, with the orientation, seals and holding method in EM-23–25.
Reinstall the other assemblies removed for cam pulley access.

completionChecks.text: Both camshaft timing pulleys installed and torqued to the manual's values.

steps.title: Connect the belt and set the tensioner
instructions: After the specified pulley positioning, connect the belt to the camshaft pulleys while keeping the crankshaft-to-intake run free of slack.
Compress the tensioner slowly in a press and hold it with the retaining pin. Fit it with the dust boot, tighten the two bolts alternately, then withdraw the pin.

cautions.text: Compress the tensioner slowly. Do not exceed the force in the manual.

completionChecks.text: Retaining pin withdrawn after both bolts are tightened.
No slack between the crankshaft and intake camshaft pulleys.

gaps: Belt tooth count, pitch and wrap angles are not modeled.

steps.title: Verify valve timing
instructions: Turn the crankshaft slowly clockwise through two revolutions from TDC to TDC.
Check that every timing mark aligns as the manual shows. If any mark disagrees, remove and reinstall the belt.

cautions.text: Stop if you feel resistance while turning. Do not force the crankshaft.

completionChecks.text: All marks align after two revolutions.

gaps: Timing marks are not modeled. Use the factory diagrams.

steps.title: Reassemble
instructions: Tighten the crankshaft pulley bolt with the holding tool to the specified torque.
Reinstall the upper cover, accessory tensioner, power-steering pump and bracket, accessory belt, radiator assembly and under-cover. Refill the coolant.

completionChecks.text: Crankshaft pulley bolt torqued to the manual's value.
All removed assemblies reinstalled.

finalChecks.text: Valve timing verified after two crankshaft revolutions.
Coolant refilled, leaks checked and level rechecked as specified.
Accessory belt routed and tensioned per the manual.
No tools, rags or fasteners left in the engine bay (general workshop practice).
